newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria may introduce currency board in June.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria may introduce currency board in June.

text.p: Bulgaria's central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Tuesday that a restrictive currency mechanism, the currency board, proposed by the IMF to stabilise the crumbling economy can be introduced in June.

"The normal introduction of a currency board can happen in June because in the name of political forces, vital stabilisation measures were postponed so far," Filipov told reporters at Sofia airport on arrival from the Bank of International Settlements annual meeting in Basle.

"Stabilisation measures, which may include a fixed exchange rate, can be introduced before the implementation of the currency board, if the needed financial resources for this are available," said Filipov.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) proposed the implementation of a currency board last year to halt the freefall of the national currency, the lev, and to restore confidence in ailing banks.
The system requires levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely curbing financial powers of the government and the central bank.
Opposition demands for early elections and the refusal of the ruling ex-communists to yield produced a political deadlock which was resolved after 30 days of mass protests.
President Petar Stoyanov, elected on the opposition ticket in November, brokered an agreement a week ago to hold early polls by April 20.
Filipov said the IMF had been prepared to introduce the currency board in January but the political instability delayed the negotiations.
The IMF had said it was prepared to resume talks as soon as an interim government was in place.
